activity.notes: Representative c.630 intellectual point under the influential c.600–660 reconstruction, not an asserted exact event or uncontested lifespan date. SEP explicitly warns that sixth- versus seventh-century dating remains debated, while Tibetan sources place Dharmakīrti at Nālandā. Oxford's standard reference chronology gives c.600–660, and Oxford's history of Harsha describes Nālandā as a major Buddhist centre during Harsha's 606–647 reign. ATLAS therefore records a Vardhana Empire active_in rail at disputed confidence so the chronological controversy remains visible rather than being silently resolved.
